appearances.name: Huajiang Canyon Bridge

It has a total length of 2,890 meters and a main span of 1,420 meters. See changelog update .

appearances.name: Duge Bridge
appearances.title: 2. Duge Bridge (China)
appearances.description: The Duge Bridge , also known as the Beipanjiang Bridge, was the world's highest bridge from 2016 until 2025, towering 565 meters above the Beipan River. It is part of the G56 Hangzhou-Ruili Expressway and cut travel time between Xuanwei and Shuicheng from over 4 hours to about 1 hour. It was surpassed by the Huajiang Canyon Bridge in September 2025. Why the record changed .

appearances.title: Duge Bridge

Stretching an astounding 164.8 kilometers (102.4 miles), this massive viaduct is a crucial segment of the Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railway. Its construction was a monumental undertaking, involving thousands of workers and advanced engineering techniques to erect the continuous box girder structure. The bridge traverses a diverse landscape, including rivers, lakes, canals, and rice paddies in the Yangtze River Delta. Its primary purpose is to support high-speed train travel, significantly reducing journey times between two of China's most important economic and cultural centers. The Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge stands as a symbol of China's rapid infrastructure development and its commitment to high-speed rail technology.

Its construction involved advanced techniques in building prestressed concrete box girders, designed to withstand seismic activity common in Taiwan. The viaduct has played a crucial role in connecting major urban centers along Taiwan's west coast, facilitating economic development, reducing travel times, and enhancing the overall transportation network of the island. It stands as a testament to Taiwan's engineering capabilities and its commitment to modernizing its infrastructure.

The Tianjin Grand Bridge plays a crucial role in facilitating rapid transportation between two of China's most important metropolitan areas, contributing significantly to economic integration and passenger convenience along this vital corridor.

appearances.significance: The Millau Viaduct, inaugurated in 2004, is not only one of the tallest bridges globally but also a remarkable feat of modern engineering and architectural design. Conceived by the French structural engineer Michel Virlogeux and the British architect Norman Foster, its slender, elegant pylons and soaring structure seamlessly blend into the landscape of the Tarn River valley. The bridge's construction overcame significant challenges, including high winds and the need to lift massive steel sections into place with exceptional precision. Its completion dramatically improved travel times between Paris and the Mediterranean coast, alleviating traffic congestion in the valley and boosting the regional economy. The Millau Viaduct has quickly become an iconic landmark of France, symbolizing innovation and the harmonious integration of human-made structures with the natural environment, attracting tourists and engineering enthusiasts alike.

technical.built: Begun in the 13th century, current structure c. 1350

appearances.significance: The Ponte delle Torri, with its current impressive structure dating back to around 1350, is a remarkable medieval bridge in Spoleto, Italy. Likely built upon Roman foundations, it not only served as a vital means of crossing the deep gorge below but also as an aqueduct, carrying water to the city. Its imposing height and the ten massive arches that support it are a testament to the engineering capabilities of the medieval period. At each end, there were originally fortified towers, giving the bridge its name ('Bridge of Towers'). Over the centuries, the Ponte delle Torri has been a symbol of Spoleto's strength and strategic importance, offering breathtaking views of the surrounding landscape and standing as a powerful reminder of the city's rich history and architectural heritage.

appearances.title: Anji Bridge
appearances.description: The Anji Bridge is the world's oldest segmental arch bridge, located in Zhao County, Hebei province, China.
appearances.significance: The Anji Bridge, completed around 605 AD during the Sui Dynasty, is the oldest segmental arch bridge in the world and a remarkable feat of ancient Chinese engineering. Designed by the craftsman Li Chun, its innovative single segmental arch design was exceptionally advanced for its time, using less material and being lighter than traditional semicircular arches, while also allowing for greater flood passage. The bridge has stood for over 1400 years, surviving numerous earthquakes and floods, a testament to the ingenuity and durability of its construction. Its elegant and efficient design influenced bridge building for centuries and remains a celebrated example of early Chinese architectural and engineering prowess.

appearances.description: The Hyde Hall Bridge is a covered bridge located in Glimmerglass State Park near Cooperstown, New York, USA.
appearances.significance: The Hyde Hall Bridge, built in 1825, is a charming covered bridge located within Glimmerglass State Park near Cooperstown, New York, USA. Constructed for George Clarke, the owner of the Hyde Hall estate, it provided a more direct route across a stream on his property. This small but historically significant covered bridge is one of the oldest surviving covered bridges in New York State. Its timber construction and simple design are characteristic of early 19th-century American covered bridges, built to protect the wooden structure from the elements and prolong its lifespan. The Hyde Hall Bridge offers a glimpse into the early transportation infrastructure of rural America and is a picturesque feature of the historic Hyde Hall estate and the surrounding landscape.

appearances.name: Manchac Swamp Bridge
appearances.title: Manchac Swamp Bridge
appearances.description: The Manchac Swamp Bridge is a twin concrete trestle bridge in Louisiana, USA.
appearances.significance: The Manchac Swamp Bridge, opened in 1979, is a twin concrete trestle bridge in Louisiana, USA. Spanning the Manchac Swamp, it carries Interstate 55 and is one of the longest overwater bridges in the world. Its construction was a significant engineering challenge due to the swamp's unique and often difficult environmental conditions. The bridge was built primarily with pilings driven deep into the swamp to provide stable support. It serves as a crucial transportation artery, connecting the areas north and south of the swamp and facilitating the movement of people and goods along I-55. The Manchac Swamp Bridge is notable not only for its length but also for the way it traverses a large and ecologically sensitive wetland environment.

appearances.name: Hangzhou Bay Bridge
appearances.title: Hangzhou Bay Bridge
appearances.description: The Hangzhou Bay Bridge is a long highway bridge across Hangzhou Bay in China.
appearances.significance: The Hangzhou Bay Bridge, opened on May 1, 2008, is an impressive cable-stayed bridge that crosses Hangzhou Bay in China. Stretching nearly 36 kilometers (about 22 miles), it was one of the longest trans-oceanic bridges in the world upon its completion. The bridge significantly shortened the travel distance between Shanghai and Ningbo, two major economic hubs in the Yangtze River Delta, boosting economic development and regional integration. Its construction was a monumental engineering feat, facing challenges such as complex tidal patterns, soft soil conditions, and the need to withstand typhoons and strong waves. The Hangzhou Bay Bridge features a unique S-shape design and includes a service island in the middle. It stands as a symbol of China's ambitious infrastructure projects and its advancements in long-span bridge construction over challenging marine environments.

appearances.title: Puente Romano (Córdoba)
appearances.description: The Puente Romano of Córdoba is a Roman bridge over the Guadalquivir river in Córdoba, Spain.
appearances.significance: The Puente Romano, dating back to the 1st century AD, is a remarkably well-preserved Roman bridge that spans the Guadalquivir River in Córdoba, Spain. Built during the Roman Empire, it was a crucial part of the ancient road network, connecting the city to the southern part of the Iberian Peninsula. For many centuries, it was the only bridge in Córdoba. Its robust construction, featuring 16 arches made of ashlar stone, has allowed it to withstand the test of time and the various floods of the Guadalquivir. The bridge has witnessed the city's transformations under Roman, Visigothic, and Moorish rule, and it remains a significant historical landmark, offering stunning views of the Mezquita-Cathedral and the city skyline. Its enduring presence serves as a powerful link to Córdoba's rich and layered past.

highestbridges.html.name: Huajiang Canyon Bridge
highestbridges.html.title: 1. Huajiang Canyon Bridge (China)
highestbridges.html.description: The Huajiang Canyon Bridge (Huajiang Grand Canyon Bridge) opened on 28 September 2025 on the S57 Liuzhi–Anlong Expressway, surpassing Duge Bridge to become the world's highest bridge deck at 625 meters above the Beipan River. It has a total length of 2,890 meters and a main span of 1,420 meters. See changelog update .

highestbridges.html.name: Duge Bridge
highestbridges.html.title: 2. Duge Bridge (China)
highestbridges.html.description: The Duge Bridge , also known as the Beipanjiang Bridge, was the world's highest bridge from 2016 until 2025, towering 565 meters above the Beipan River. It is part of the G56 Hangzhou-Ruili Expressway and cut travel time between Xuanwei and Shuicheng from over 4 hours to about 1 hour. It was surpassed by the Huajiang Canyon Bridge in September 2025. Why the record changed .

highestbridges.html.name: Tianmen Bridge
highestbridges.html.title: 3. Tianmen Bridge (China)
highestbridges.html.description: The Tianmen Bridge carries the Anpan Expressway high above the Beipan River gorge in Guizhou province with a main span of 820 meters. Completed in 2026, it ranks third among the world's highest bridges just behind Huajiang and Duge. See changelog update .

highestbridges.html.name: Sidu River Bridge
highestbridges.html.title: 4. Sidu River Bridge (China)
highestbridges.html.description: The Sidu River Bridge held the title of world's highest bridge from 2009 to 2016. Spanning the deep Sidu River valley, this suspension bridge is part of the G50 Shanghai-Chongqing Expressway and features a main span of 900 meters. Its construction required rockets to launch the initial guide cables across the gorge.

highestbridges.html.name: Puli Bridge
highestbridges.html.title: 5. Puli Bridge (China)
highestbridges.html.description: The Puli Bridge crosses the Nizhu River gorge in Yunnan province and forms part of the G56 Hangzhou-Ruili Expressway. With a main span of 628 meters, this suspension bridge connects the cities of Qujing and Kunming, dramatically improving transportation in this mountainous region.

highestbridges.html.name: Jin'an Bridge
highestbridges.html.title: 6. Jin'an Bridge (China)
highestbridges.html.description: The Jin'an Bridge spans the Jinsha River in Yunnan province and features a main span of 1,386 meters, making it one of the longest high-altitude suspension bridges in the world as well. This bridge carries the G4216 Chengdu–Lijiang (Huaping–Lijiang) Expressway and significantly improved connectivity in northwest Yunnan. Expressway name updated .

highestbridges.html.name: Yachi River Bridge
highestbridges.html.title: 7. Yachi River Bridge (China)
highestbridges.html.height: 434 m (1,424 ft) above canyon floor (306 m above reservoir)
highestbridges.html.description: The Yachi River Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge with a main span of 800 meters. It forms part of the Qianxi-Guiyang Expressway and crosses the Yachi River in Guizhou province. Its deck rises 434 meters above the original river gorge floor (306 meters above the Dongfeng Dam reservoir surface). Height baseline clarified .

highestbridges.html.name: Zangkejiang Bridge
highestbridges.html.title: 8. Zangkejiang Bridge (China)
highestbridges.html.description: The Zangkejiang Bridge opened in February 2025 as part of the Nayong–Xingyi Expressway, crossing a deep Beipan River rift with a 1,080-meter main span. See changelog update .

highestbridges.html.name: Qingshui River Bridge
highestbridges.html.title: 9. Qingshui River Bridge (China)
highestbridges.html.description: The Qingshui River Bridge spans the Qingshui River gorge with a main span of 1,130 meters. This suspension bridge is part of the Guiyang-Qianxi Expressway and features two H-shaped towers that rise dramatically from the valley below.

highestbridges.html.name: Baluarte Bridge
highestbridges.html.title: 10. Baluarte Bridge (Mexico)
highestbridges.html.description: The Baluarte Bridge is the highest bridge in the Americas and part of the Durango-Mazatlán highway. This cable-stayed bridge spans the Baluarte River and features a total length of 1,124 meters with a central span of 520 meters and a deck height of 403 meters (earlier listings cited 390 m). Following the 2018 earthquake removal of Hegigio Gorge Pipeline Bridge, Baluarte holds #10 in the updated ranking. See changelog update .

longestbridges.html.name: Danyang-Kunshan Grand Bridge
longestbridges.html.title: 1. Danyang-Kunshan Grand Bridge (China)
longestbridges.html.description: The Danyang-Kunshan Grand Bridge is the world's longest bridge, spanning across rivers, lakes, and rice paddies. It's a critical part of the Beijing-Shanghai High-Speed Railway, reducing travel time between Beijing and Shanghai from 10 hours to just 4 hours.

longestbridges.html.name: Changhua-Kaohsiung Viaduct
longestbridges.html.title: 2. Changhua-Kaohsiung Viaduct (Taiwan)
longestbridges.html.description: This viaduct is a key segment of Taiwan's high-speed rail network, connecting major cities while withstanding frequent earthquakes. It forms the longest part of the Taiwan High Speed Rail line, which runs along the west coast of the island.

longestbridges.html.name: Kita-Yaita Viaduct
longestbridges.html.title: 3. Kita-Yaita Viaduct (Japan)
longestbridges.html.description: The Kita-Yaita Viaduct on Japan's Tōhoku Shinkansen stretches 114.4 kilometers across Tochigi Prefecture, making it the longest railway viaduct outside China and third longest bridge overall. Added in changelog update .

longestbridges.html.name: Tianjin Grand Bridge
longestbridges.html.title: 4. Tianjin Grand Bridge (China)
longestbridges.html.description: Another marvel of China's rail infrastructure, this viaduct runs between Langfang and Qingxian in Hebei while passing through Tianjin municipality. It crosses diverse terrain including rivers, highways, and urban areas on the Beijing-Shanghai High-Speed Railway. Location clarified .

longestbridges.html.name: Cangde Grand Bridge
longestbridges.html.title: 5. Cangde Grand Bridge (China)
longestbridges.html.description: Built to support high-speed trains, this bridge showcases China's expertise in large-scale infrastructure projects. Completed in 2010 and opened to rail service on June 30, 2011, it forms part of the Beijing-Shanghai High-Speed Railway using prefabricated sections. Opening year corrected .

longestbridges.html.name: Weinan Weihe Grand Bridge
longestbridges.html.title: 6. Weinan Weihe Grand Bridge (China)
longestbridges.html.description: This bridge crosses the Wei River twice and was briefly the longest bridge in the world upon completion in 2008 before opening with the Zhengzhou-Xi'an High-Speed Railway in February 2010. Opening year corrected .

longestbridges.html.name: Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge
longestbridges.html.title: 7. Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge (China)
longestbridges.html.description: Opened in October 2018, the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge spans the Pearl River Estuary, combining nearly 50 kilometers of over-water bridge viaducts and cable-stayed spans with an undersea tunnel and artificial islands. Added in changelog update .

longestbridges.html.name: Bang Na Expressway
longestbridges.html.title: 8. Bang Na Expressway (Thailand)
longestbridges.html.description: One of the longest road bridges, it helps alleviate traffic congestion in Bangkok by providing an elevated route. The six-lane expressway runs above the existing Bang Na-Trat Highway and was the world's longest road bridge until 2008.

longestbridges.html.name: Beijing Grand Bridge
longestbridges.html.title: 9. Beijing Grand Bridge (China)
longestbridges.html.description: Part of the Beijing-Shanghai High-Speed Railway, this bridge ensures smooth and rapid transit across northern China. It was constructed using advanced pre-stressed concrete technology to support high-speed train operations.

longestbridges.html.name: Lake Pontchartrain Causeway
longestbridges.html.title: 10. Lake Pontchartrain Causeway (USA)
longestbridges.html.description: This iconic U.S. bridge holds the Guinness World Record for the longest continuous bridge over water. The twin parallel bridges cross Lake Pontchartrain in southern Louisiana, connecting Metairie with Mandeville. (Manchac Swamp Bridge and Yangcun Bridge remain featured in our History and Gallery sections; see changelog .)

tallestbridges.html.name: Changtai Yangtze River Bridge
tallestbridges.html.title: 1. Changtai Yangtze River Bridge (China)
tallestbridges.html.description: Opened on 9 September 2025, the Changtai Yangtze River Bridge connects Changzhou and Taizhou with diamond-shaped pylons rising 352 meters—surpassing the Millau Viaduct as the world's tallest bridge structure—alongside the world's longest cable-stayed main span at 1,176 meters. See changelog update .

tallestbridges.html.name: Ma'anshan Yangtze River Rail-Road Bridge
tallestbridges.html.title: 2. Ma'anshan Yangtze River Rail-Road Bridge (China)
tallestbridges.html.description: The Ma'anshan Yangtze River Rail-Road Bridge is a three-tower, dual 1,120-meter main-span cable-stayed crossing carrying both expressway and high-speed rail decks, with its middle tower reaching approximately 345 meters (structural closure achieved in 2025 ahead of full 2026 operations). See changelog update .

tallestbridges.html.name: Millau Viaduct
tallestbridges.html.title: 3. Millau Viaduct (France)
tallestbridges.html.description: The Millau Viaduct held the record as the tallest bridge in the world from 2004 until 2025, spanning the Tarn River Valley in southern France. Its tallest mast reaches 343 meters (1,125 ft) above the valley floor, taller than the Eiffel Tower, before being surpassed by China's Changtai Yangtze River Bridge. Why the ranking changed .

tallestbridges.html.name: 1915 Çanakkale Bridge
tallestbridges.html.title: 4. 1915 Çanakkale Bridge (Turkey)
tallestbridges.html.height: 334 m (1,096 ft) (318 m towers + 16 m ornaments)
tallestbridges.html.description: The 1915 Çanakkale Bridge connects the European and Asian sides of Turkey across the Dardanelles Strait. It's the longest suspension bridge in the world with a main span of 2,023 meters (6,637 ft).

tallestbridges.html.name: Pingtang Bridge
tallestbridges.html.title: 5. Pingtang Bridge (China)
tallestbridges.html.description: The Pingtang Bridge features the tallest concrete bridge tower in the world (332 m) supporting dual 550-meter main spans with a steel-concrete composite girder deck across the Caodu River canyon in Guizhou province. Deck type corrected .

tallestbridges.html.name: Husutong Yangtze River Bridge
tallestbridges.html.title: 6. Husutong Yangtze River Bridge (China)
tallestbridges.html.description: The Husutong Yangtze River Bridge is a combined rail and road bridge that forms a critical link in China's transportation network. Its height allows large ships to pass underneath on the busy Yangtze River. Opening year corrected to 2020. See the fact update .

tallestbridges.html.name: Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge
tallestbridges.html.title: 7. Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge (Turkey)
tallestbridges.html.description: The Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge is a hybrid cable-stayed suspension bridge that carries both highway and railway traffic across the Bosphorus. It's the third bridge connecting the European and Asian sides of Istanbul. Type metadata updated .

tallestbridges.html.name: Russky Bridge
tallestbridges.html.title: 8. Russky Bridge (Russia)
tallestbridges.html.description: The Russky Bridge connects Russky Island to the mainland near Vladivostok. Built for the 2012 APEC summit, it features one of the longest cable-stayed spans in the world at 1,104 meters (3,622 ft).

tallestbridges.html.name: Sutong Bridge
tallestbridges.html.title: 9. Sutong Bridge (China)
tallestbridges.html.description: The Sutong Bridge was the world's longest cable-stayed bridge when completed, with a main span of 1,088 meters (3,570 ft). It crosses the Yangtze River and significantly reduced travel time between Nantong and Suzhou.

tallestbridges.html.name: Stonecutters Bridge
tallestbridges.html.title: 10. Stonecutters Bridge (Hong Kong)
tallestbridges.html.description: The Stonecutters Bridge is a landmark cable-stayed bridge in Hong Kong, opened to traffic in December 2009. Its innovative design features twin single-leg towers that lean outwards, creating a distinctive silhouette against the Hong Kong skyline. (Chishi Bridge and the 2021 Zunyu Expressway Xiang River Bridge in Guizhou now sit just outside the Top 10; see changelog .)

oldestbridges.html.name: Arkadiko Bridge
oldestbridges.html.title: 1. Arkadiko Bridge (Greece)
oldestbridges.html.description: The Arkadiko Bridge is one of the oldest surviving arch bridges in the world, dating back to the Bronze Age. This Mycenaean bridge is still standing after more than 3,000 years, built using Cyclopean masonry techniques.

oldestbridges.html.name: Tarr Steps
oldestbridges.html.title: 2. Tarr Steps (UK)
oldestbridges.html.built: c. 1400 AD (medieval; popularly cited as 1000 BC)
oldestbridges.html.description: The Tarr Steps is a historic clapper bridge made of massive stone slabs resting on stone piers across the River Barle. While local tradition and early accounts date it to 1000 BC, archaeological and heritage assessments largely date the surviving structure to the medieval period (around 1400 AD). Dating note added .

oldestbridges.html.name: Bridge Over River Meles
oldestbridges.html.title: 3. Bridge Over River Meles (Turkey)
oldestbridges.html.description: This ancient bridge over the River Meles is associated with the famous poet Homer, who is said to have composed his works near this location. The bridge represents early stone arch construction techniques.

oldestbridges.html.name: Pons Fabricius
oldestbridges.html.title: 4. Pons Fabricius (Italy)
oldestbridges.html.description: The Pons Fabricius is the oldest Roman bridge in Rome still in its original state. Built by Lucius Fabricius, it connects Tiber Island to the left bank of the Tiber River and remains open to pedestrians after 2,000 years.

oldestbridges.html.name: Alcántara Bridge
oldestbridges.html.title: 5. Alcántara Bridge (Spain)
oldestbridges.html.description: The Alcántara Bridge is a masterpiece of Roman engineering, built under Emperor Trajan. Spanning the Tagus River, its central arch rises 45 meters above the water, demonstrating advanced Roman construction techniques.

oldestbridges.html.name: Ponte Sant'Angelo
oldestbridges.html.title: 6. Ponte Sant'Angelo (Italy)
oldestbridges.html.description: Originally built as the Aelian Bridge by Emperor Hadrian, Ponte Sant'Angelo connects central Rome with the Castel Sant'Angelo. The bridge is adorned with magnificent Baroque statues added in the 17th century.

oldestbridges.html.name: Cendere Bridge
oldestbridges.html.title: 7. Cendere Bridge (Turkey)
oldestbridges.html.description: The Cendere Bridge is one of the best-preserved Roman bridges, built by the XVI Legion during the reign of Septimius Severus. This single-arch bridge spans the Cendere River and is still walkable today.

oldestbridges.html.name: Band-e Kaisar
oldestbridges.html.title: 8. Band-e Kaisar (Iran)
oldestbridges.html.description: Band-e Kaisar ("Caesar's Bridge") was built by Roman engineers captured after the Battle of Edessa. This unique structure served as both a bridge and a dam, demonstrating Roman hydraulic engineering in Persia.

oldestbridges.html.name: Bridge near Limyra
oldestbridges.html.title: 9. Bridge near Limyra (Turkey)
oldestbridges.html.description: This ancient bridge near Limyra is one of the oldest segmented arch bridges still visible today. Its flattened arch design represents an important development in bridge engineering history.

oldestbridges.html.name: Karamagara Bridge
oldestbridges.html.title: 10. Karamagara Bridge (Turkey)
oldestbridges.html.description: The Karamagara Bridge was a remarkable feat of Byzantine engineering, featuring one of the earliest known pointed arches. Unfortunately, the bridge is now submerged under the Keban Dam reservoir.

highestbridges_modal.title: Huajiang Canyon Bridge (~625 m)
highestbridges_modal.description: Opened in September 2025 over China's Beipan River, the Huajiang Canyon Bridge now holds the #1 highest deck record (~625 m), surpassing Duge Bridge (565 m).

gallery.html.name: Millau Viaduct
gallery.html.title: Millau Viaduct
gallery.html.description: The world's tallest bridge with its tallest pylon at 343 meters. This cable-stayed bridge spans the Tarn River valley in France, completed in 2004. It handles approximately 28,000 vehicles daily and has become a global tourist attraction.

gallery.html.name: Pingtang Bridge
gallery.html.title: Pingtang Bridge
gallery.html.description: A 2,135-meter cable-stayed bridge crossing a deep valley in China's Guizhou Province. Completed in 2019, it features a 550-meter main span and enhances accessibility in China's mountainous southwest.

gallery.html.name: Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge
gallery.html.title: Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge
gallery.html.description: A hybrid suspension bridge spanning the Bosphorus in Istanbul, completed in 2016. With 322-meter pylons, it accommodates both highway and rail traffic, handling over 200,000 vehicles daily.

gallery.html.name: Russky Bridge
gallery.html.title: Russky Bridge
gallery.html.description: Connects Vladivostok to Russky Island with a record-breaking 1,104-meter main span. Completed in 2012, this cable-stayed bridge withstands typhoons and subzero temperatures.

gallery.html.name: Sutong Yangtze River Bridge
gallery.html.title: Sutong Yangtze River Bridge
gallery.html.description: An 8,206-meter cable-stayed bridge crossing the Yangtze River in China. Completed in 2008, it features 306-meter pylons and supports 80,000 vehicles daily on the G15 Shenhai Expressway.

gallery.html.name: Stonecutters Bridge
gallery.html.title: Stonecutters Bridge
gallery.html.description: A cable-stayed bridge spanning Hong Kong's Rambler Channel, completed in 2009. Its 298-meter pylons and 1,018-meter main span support 80,000 vehicles daily on Route 8.

gallery.html.name: Akashi Kaikyo Bridge
gallery.html.title: Akashi Kaikyo Bridge
gallery.html.description: Held the record as the world's longest suspension bridge (1,991-meter main span) from 1998 until surpassed by the 1915 Çanakkale Bridge in 2022. It links Kobe to Awaji Island in Japan and withstands earthquakes and typhoons.

gallery.html.name: Jingyue Bridge
gallery.html.title: Jingyue Bridge
gallery.html.description: A cable-stayed bridge crossing the Yangtze River in Hubei, China. Completed in 2010, its 280-meter pylons and 816-meter main span support 60,000 vehicles daily on the G56 Expressway.

gallery.html.name: Tatara Bridge
gallery.html.title: Tatara Bridge
gallery.html.description: A cable-stayed bridge spanning Japan's Seto Inland Sea between Honshu and Shikoku. Completed in 1999, its 220-meter pylons and 890-meter main span were record-breaking at the time.

gallery.html.name: Great Belt East Bridge
gallery.html.title: Great Belt East Bridge
gallery.html.description: A suspension bridge linking Zealand and Funen in Denmark. Completed in 1998, its 254-meter pylons and 1,624-meter main span reduced travel time between Copenhagen and Funen from 90 minutes to 10.

gallery.html.name: Duge Bridge
gallery.html.title: Duge Bridge
gallery.html.description: The world's highest bridge with a deck 565 meters above the Beipan River in China. Completed in 2016, this 1,340-meter cable-stayed bridge connects Yunnan and Guizhou provinces.

gallery.html.name: Sidu River Bridge
gallery.html.title: Sidu River Bridge
gallery.html.description: One of the world's highest bridges at 496 meters above the Sidu River valley. Completed in 2009, this suspension bridge forms part of the G50 Shanghai-Chongqing Expressway in China.

gallery.html.name: Puli Bridge
gallery.html.title: Puli Bridge
gallery.html.description: A suspension bridge with a deck 485 meters above a valley in Yunnan, China. Completed in 2015, it forms part of the G56 Hangzhou-Ruili Expressway, connecting remote regions.

gallery.html.name: Qingshuihe Bridge
gallery.html.title: Qingshuihe Bridge
gallery.html.description: A suspension bridge with a deck 406 meters above the Qingshui River in China. Completed in 2015, its 2,171-meter span forms part of the G60 Shanghai-Kunming Expressway.

gallery.html.name: Baling River Bridge
gallery.html.title: Baling River Bridge
gallery.html.description: A suspension bridge with a deck 370 meters above the Baling River in China. Completed in 2009, its 2,237-meter span supports 25,000 vehicles daily on the G60 Expressway.

gallery.html.name: Beipanjiang Bridge (Guanxing Highway)
gallery.html.title: Beipanjiang Bridge (Guanxing Highway)
gallery.html.description: A suspension bridge with a deck 366 meters above the Beipan River in China (388-meter main span). Completed in 2003, it was the world's first bridge to exceed 300 meters in deck height.

gallery.html.name: Liuguanghe Bridge
gallery.html.title: Liuguanghe Bridge
gallery.html.description: A beam bridge with a deck 297 meters above the Liuguang River in China. Completed in 2001, this 580-meter bridge was among the highest in the world at the time.

gallery.html.name: Yachi River Bridge
gallery.html.title: Yachi River Bridge
gallery.html.description: A cable-stayed bridge with a deck 306 meters above the Dongfeng Dam reservoir (434 meters above the original canyon floor) in China. Completed in 2016, its 1,444-meter span supports 30,000 vehicles daily on the Expressway.

gallery.html.name: Royal Gorge Bridge
gallery.html.title: Royal Gorge Bridge
gallery.html.description: A historic suspension bridge 291 meters above the Arkansas River in Colorado. Completed in 1929 as a tourist attraction, it now draws 500,000 visitors annually to its pedestrian walkway.

gallery.html.name: Zhijinghe River Bridge
gallery.html.title: Zhijinghe River Bridge
gallery.html.description: An arch bridge with a deck 294 meters above the Zhijinghe River in China. Completed in 2009, this 430-meter bridge forms part of the G50 Shanghai-Chongqing Expressway.

gallery.html.name: Alcantara Bridge
gallery.html.title: Alcantara Bridge
gallery.html.description: One of the world's oldest bridges still in use, completed in 106 AD in Spain near the Portuguese border. This Roman stone arch bridge spans the Tagus River with six granite arches built without mortar.

gallery.html.name: Ponte Fabricio
gallery.html.title: Ponte Fabricio
gallery.html.description: Rome's oldest bridge still in use, completed in 62 BC. This 62-meter stone arch bridge connects the city center with Tiber Island and has survived floods and invasions.

gallery.html.name: Ponte di Tiberio
gallery.html.title: Ponte di Tiberio
gallery.html.description: A Roman stone arch bridge completed in 20 AD in Rimini, Italy. This 70-meter bridge with five arches was a vital link in the Via Emilia, connecting Rome to northern Italy.

gallery.html.name: Ponte Vecchio
gallery.html.title: Ponte Vecchio
gallery.html.description: A medieval stone arch bridge spanning the Arno River in Florence, completed in 1345. Famous for its shops housing jewelers and artisans, it's a major tourist attraction.

gallery.html.name: Charles Bridge
gallery.html.title: Charles Bridge
gallery.html.description: A Gothic stone arch bridge spanning the Vltava River in Prague, completed in 1402. Adorned with 30 Baroque statues, it's a vibrant pedestrian hub and major tourist attraction.

gallery.html.name: Rialto Bridge
gallery.html.title: Rialto Bridge
gallery.html.description: A Renaissance stone arch bridge spanning Venice's Grand Canal, completed in 1591. Its single 22-meter arch and iconic shops make it one of Venice's most famous landmarks.

gallery.html.name: Ponte delle Torri
gallery.html.title: Ponte delle Torri
gallery.html.description: A medieval stone arch bridge in Spoleto, Italy, originally serving as an aqueduct. Completed around 1350, this 230-meter bridge features 10 Gothic arches spanning the Tessino valley.

gallery.html.name: Puente Romano (Mérida)
gallery.html.title: Puente Romano (Mérida)
gallery.html.description: One of the world's oldest bridges still in use, built by the Romans in the 1st century AD. This 790-meter stone arch bridge spans the Guadiana River in Mérida, Spain.

gallery.html.name: Anji Bridge
gallery.html.title: Anji Bridge
gallery.html.description: One of the world's oldest stone arch bridges still in use, completed in 605 AD in China. This 50-meter bridge features an innovative open-spandrel design with a 37-meter segmental arch.

gallery.html.name: Hyde Hall Bridge
gallery.html.title: Hyde Hall Bridge
gallery.html.description: One of the oldest covered wooden bridges still in use in the USA, completed in 1825. This 16-meter bridge in Cooperstown, New York features a Burr arch truss design.

gallery.html.name: Danyang-Kunshan Grand Bridge
gallery.html.title: Danyang-Kunshan Grand Bridge
gallery.html.description: The world's longest bridge at 164.8 kilometers, part of China's Beijing-Shanghai High-Speed Railway. Completed in 2011, this viaduct handles 80 million passengers annually, reducing travel time from 10 hours to 4.

gallery.html.name: Changhua-Kaohsiung Viaduct
gallery.html.title: Changhua-Kaohsiung Viaduct
gallery.html.description: The world's second-longest bridge at 157.3 kilometers, part of Taiwan's High-Speed Rail. Completed in 2007, it reduced travel time between Taipei and Kaohsiung from 4.5 hours to 1.5.

gallery.html.name: Tianjin Grand Bridge
gallery.html.title: Tianjin Grand Bridge
gallery.html.description: One of the world's longest bridges at 113.7 kilometers, part of China's Beijing-Shanghai High-Speed Railway. Completed in 2011, this viaduct handles 80 million passengers annually.

gallery.html.name: Cangde Grand Bridge
gallery.html.title: Cangde Grand Bridge
gallery.html.description: A 105.8-kilometer viaduct bridge part of China's Beijing-Shanghai High-Speed Railway. Completed in 2010 and opened in 2011, it navigates soft soil and urban areas while supporting high-speed trains at 300 km/h.

gallery.html.name: Weinan Weihe Grand Bridge
gallery.html.title: Weinan Weihe Grand Bridge
gallery.html.description: A 79.7-kilometer viaduct bridge part of China's Zhengzhou-Xi'an High-Speed Railway. Completed in 2008 and opened in 2010, it reduced travel time between Zhengzhou and Xi'an from 6 hours to 2.

gallery.html.name: Bang Na Expressway
gallery.html.title: Bang Na Expressway
gallery.html.description: A 54-kilometer elevated viaduct bridge across Bangkok, Thailand. Completed in 2000, it supports 120,000 vehicles daily and reduced travel time across the city by 30 minutes.

gallery.html.name: Beijing Grand Bridge
gallery.html.title: Beijing Grand Bridge
gallery.html.description: A 48.2-kilometer viaduct bridge part of China's Beijing-Shanghai High-Speed Railway. Completed in 2011, it handles 80 million passengers annually while navigating urban areas and soft soil.

gallery.html.name: Manchac Swamp Bridge
gallery.html.title: Manchac Swamp Bridge
gallery.html.description: A 36.7-kilometer viaduct bridge across Louisiana's Manchac Swamp. Completed in 1979, this part of Interstate 55 supports 35,000 vehicles daily while preserving wetland ecosystems.

gallery.html.name: Hangzhou Bay Bridge
gallery.html.title: Hangzhou Bay Bridge
gallery.html.description: A 35.7-kilometer cable-stayed bridge across China's Hangzhou Bay. Completed in 2008, its S-shaped design supports 50,000 vehicles daily, reducing travel time between Shanghai and Ningbo from 4 hours to 2.

history.html.name: Sutong Yangtze River Bridge
history.html.title: Sutong Yangtze River Bridge
history.html.description: The Sutong Yangtze River Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge across the Yangtze River in China between Nantong and Suzhou.
history.html.significance: Opened in 2008, the Sutong Yangtze River Bridge was a groundbreaking achievement in cable-stayed bridge technology, holding the record for the longest span of its kind upon completion. Spanning the vast and busy Yangtze River, it significantly improved connectivity between the major economic centers of Nantong and Suzhou, playing a crucial role in regional development and economic integration. The construction of this massive bridge involved overcoming significant engineering challenges, including deepwater foundations and the erection of its tall towers in a seismically active zone. The Sutong Bridge stands as a symbol of China's rapid infrastructure development and its leadership in long-span bridge construction, facilitating trade and travel across one of the country's most vital waterways. Its innovative design and construction techniques have contributed significantly to the advancement of bridge engineering worldwide.

history.html.name: Stonecutters Bridge
history.html.title: Stonecutters Bridge
history.html.description: The Stonecutters Bridge is a high cable-stayed bridge spanning the Rambler Channel in Hong Kong.
history.html.significance: Opened in 2009, the Stonecutters Bridge is an iconic and vital part of Hong Kong's infrastructure. Its striking design features two tall, slender towers that support a long central span over the busy Rambler Channel, connecting the Kwai Chung container terminals and the new Hong Kong International Airport on Lantau Island. The bridge's construction was a significant engineering undertaking, requiring innovative techniques to manage the soft marine clay at the seabed and to erect the massive pre-fabricated deck segments. Its completion significantly improved transportation efficiency, reduced travel times, and enhanced the connectivity of key economic hubs in Hong Kong. The Stonecutters Bridge has also become a recognizable landmark in the city's skyline, symbolizing modern engineering and Hong Kong's status as a major global trade and logistics center.

history.html.name: Akashi Kaikyo Bridge
history.html.title: Akashi Kaikyo Bridge
history.html.description: The Akashi Kaikyō Bridge is a suspension bridge which links Kobe on Honshu island to Awaji Island in Japan.
history.html.significance: The Akashi Kaikyō Bridge, opened in 1998, is a monumental engineering achievement and held the title of the world's longest suspension bridge for many years. Linking the city of Kobe on Honshu island with Awaji Island across the turbulent Akashi Strait, its construction was driven by the need to improve transportation safety and efficiency in a region prone to severe weather and earthquakes. The bridge was designed with exceptional resilience, capable of withstanding winds of up to 286 km/h and earthquakes with a magnitude of 8.5. Its construction involved groundbreaking techniques in cable spinning and tower erection. The Akashi Kaikyō Bridge is a symbol of Japan's advanced engineering capabilities and its commitment to overcoming geographical challenges to connect its islands, playing a crucial role in the regional economy and transportation network.

history.html.name: Millau Viaduct
history.html.title: Millau Viaduct
history.html.description: The Millau Viaduct is a cable-stayed bridge that spans the valley of the River Tarn near Millau in Southern France.
history.html.significance: The Millau Viaduct, inaugurated in 2004, is not only one of the tallest bridges globally but also a remarkable feat of modern engineering and architectural design. Conceived by the French structural engineer Michel Virlogeux and the British architect Norman Foster, its slender, elegant pylons and soaring structure seamlessly blend into the landscape of the Tarn River valley. The bridge's construction overcame significant challenges, including high winds and the need to lift massive steel sections into place with exceptional precision. Its completion dramatically improved travel times between Paris and the Mediterranean coast, alleviating traffic congestion in the valley and boosting the regional economy. The Millau Viaduct has quickly become an iconic landmark of France, symbolizing innovation and the harmonious integration of human-made structures with the natural environment, attracting tourists and engineering enthusiasts alike.

history.html.name: Pingtang Bridge
history.html.title: Pingtang Bridge
history.html.description: The Pingtang Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge with the tallest concrete bridge tower in the world, located in Guizhou, China.
history.html.significance: The Pingtang Bridge, opened in late 2019, is a monumental engineering achievement, most notably for housing the tallest concrete bridge tower ever constructed. Located in the mountainous Guizhou province of China, its construction presented immense logistical and technical hurdles due to the challenging terrain and remote location. The bridge forms a crucial part of the Pingtang-Luodian Expressway, significantly reducing travel times and improving connectivity in a historically underdeveloped region. Beyond its functional importance, the Pingtang Bridge stands as a testament to China's advancements in bridge construction technology and its commitment to developing infrastructure in its western provinces. The sheer scale of the structure and the record-breaking height of its main tower have garnered international attention from the engineering community and highlight the capabilities of modern concrete construction in extreme environments.

history.html.name: Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge
history.html.title: Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge
history.html.description: The Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge is a combined road-rail bridge over the Bosphorus strait, north of the two existing suspension bridges in Istanbul, Turkey.
history.html.significance: The Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge, inaugurated in 2016, holds the distinction of being a unique hybrid bridge, combining cable-stayed and suspension bridge elements to carry both vehicular and railway traffic across the strategic Bosphorus Strait in Istanbul. Named after the 16th-century Ottoman Sultan Selim I, its construction aimed to alleviate the heavy traffic congestion on the existing Bosphorus bridges and to enhance transportation links between the European and Asian sides of Turkey. The bridge's impressive height and long span made it a significant engineering undertaking, employing advanced construction techniques to withstand seismic activity and strong currents in the strait. Its completion marked a major infrastructure development for Istanbul, contributing to economic growth and facilitating smoother transit across this vital waterway that connects the Black Sea and the Mediterranean. The bridge stands as a symbol of Turkey's modern engineering capabilities and its role as a crucial geographical and economic crossroads.

history.html.name: Russky Bridge
history.html.title: Russky Bridge
history.html.description: The Russky Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge in Vladivostok, Russia that connects the mainland to Russky Island across the Eastern Bosphorus strait.
history.html.significance: The Russky Bridge, completed in 2012, is an iconic structure in Vladivostok, Russia, built to connect the mainland with Russky Island in preparation for the APEC summit. For a period, it held the record for the world's longest cable-stayed bridge span, showcasing remarkable engineering prowess in a region known for its challenging climate, including ice formation and strong winds. The bridge's construction significantly improved accessibility to Russky Island, opening it up for further development, education (housing a Far Eastern Federal University campus), and tourism. Its towering pylons, shaped like inverted 'V's, have become a symbol of modern Vladivostok and a testament to Russia's ability to undertake large-scale infrastructure projects in demanding environments. The bridge plays a vital role in the regional transportation network and stands as an impressive example of contemporary bridge design and construction.

history.html.name: Jingyue Bridge
history.html.title: Jingyue Bridge
history.html.description: The Jingyue Yangtze River Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge crossing the Yangtze River between Jianli (Hubei) and Yueyang (Hunan), China.
history.html.significance: Opened in June 2010, the Jingyue Yangtze River Bridge is a major asymmetric cable-stayed crossing spanning the Yangtze River between Jianli in Hubei Province and Yueyang in Hunan Province. Its 816-meter main span ranked among the longest cable-stayed spans in the world at the time of completion. Carrying the G0421 Xuchang–Guangzhou Expressway across six lanes, it plays a vital role in regional connectivity and freight transport across central China.

history.html.name: Tatara Bridge
history.html.title: Tatara Bridge
history.html.description: The Tatara Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge that is part of the Nishiseto Expressway, linking Honshu and Shikoku islands across the Seto Inland Sea in Japan.
history.html.significance: The Tatara Bridge, opened in 1999, is a prominent cable-stayed bridge that forms a crucial link in the Nishiseto Expressway, connecting the islands of Honshu and Shikoku in Japan. For a time, it held the distinction of having the second-longest cable-stayed span in the world. Its construction was a significant undertaking, contributing to the comprehensive network of bridges that have integrated the economies and communities of the Seto Inland Sea region. The Tatara Bridge is not only an impressive feat of engineering but also a visually striking structure that blends harmoniously with the scenic beauty of the Japanese coastline, enhancing transportation and promoting tourism in the area.

history.html.name: Great Belt East Bridge
history.html.title: Great Belt East Bridge
history.html.description: The Great Belt East Bridge is a suspension bridge that forms part of the Great Belt Fixed Link connecting the Danish islands of Zealand and Funen.
history.html.significance: The Great Belt East Bridge, inaugurated in 1998, is a vital component of the Great Belt Fixed Link, a monumental infrastructure project that dramatically improved transportation between the eastern and western parts of Denmark. As a suspension bridge with one of the longest main spans in the world, its construction was a remarkable engineering achievement, facing challenges from strong winds and deep waters. The completion of the bridge significantly reduced travel times, fostering greater economic integration and social cohesion across the Danish islands of Zealand and Funen. It stands as a symbol of Denmark's commitment to advanced engineering and its impact on national connectivity and development.

history.html.name: Qingshuihe Bridge
history.html.title: Qingshuihe Bridge
history.html.description: The Qingshuihe Bridge is a suspension bridge in Guizhou province, China.
history.html.significance: The Qingshuihe Bridge, inaugurated at the close of 2015, represents a significant advancement in suspension bridge engineering within the challenging geographical landscape of Guizhou province, China. Its impressive height, soaring over the deep Qingshui River valley, underscores the ambition and technical capabilities involved in its construction. As a crucial component of the regional expressway network, the bridge has played a transformative role in improving transportation efficiency, reducing travel times across this previously difficult terrain, and fostering greater economic integration for the communities it serves. The sheer scale of its main span, exceeding a kilometer, along with the innovative construction methodologies employed, solidifies its place as a remarkable achievement in modern infrastructure development in southwestern China.

history.html.name: Baling River Bridge
history.html.title: Baling River Bridge
history.html.description: The Baling River Bridge is a suspension bridge over the Baling River in Guizhou province, China.
history.html.significance: The Baling River Bridge, opened in the final days of 2009, stands as a testament to the engineering prowess required to bridge the deep Baling River valley in Guizhou province, China. Its construction was a monumental undertaking that significantly enhanced the transportation infrastructure of a region marked by challenging topography. At the time of its completion, its towering height above the riverbed placed it among the world's highest bridges. As a vital link on the G60 Shanghai–Kunming Expressway, the bridge has dramatically reduced travel times, facilitated the movement of goods and people, and spurred economic growth in previously isolated areas. Its impressive length and the advanced suspension technology employed in its creation underscore China's rapid development in large-scale infrastructure projects and its commitment to connecting its diverse regions.

history.html.name: Beipanjiang Bridge (Guanxing Highway)
history.html.title: Beipanjiang Bridge (Guanxing Highway)
history.html.description: The Beipanjiang Bridge on the Guanxing Highway is a suspension bridge in Guizhou province, China.
history.html.significance: The Beipanjiang Bridge, which opened on the Guanxing Highway in late 2003, is a landmark suspension bridge spanning the deep Beipan River valley in Guizhou province, China. Upon completion it became the world's highest bridge and the first to exceed 300 meters in deck height, dramatically improving transportation links across Guizhou's mountainous terrain.

history.html.name: Liuguanghe Bridge
history.html.title: Liuguanghe Bridge
history.html.description: The 2001 Liuguanghe Bridge is a prestressed concrete beam bridge in Guizhou province, China (distinct from the 2017 Liuguanghe Xiqian Expressway cable-stayed bridge).
history.html.significance: The Liuguanghe Bridge, completed in 2001, is a pioneering prestressed concrete beam bridge located in Guizhou province, China, crossing the Liuguang River. At 297 meters above the river, it held the world's highest bridge record from 2001 until 2003. (It should not be confused with the nearby 2017 Liuguanghe Xiqian Expressway cable-stayed bridge, which rises 375 meters with a 580-meter span.)

history.html.name: Yachi River Bridge
history.html.title: Yachi River Bridge
history.html.description: The Yachi River Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge in Guizhou province, China.

technical.height: 306 meters (1,004 ft) above reservoir (434 m above original canyon floor)

history.html.significance: The Yachi River Bridge, completed in 2016, is a notable example of modern cable-stayed bridge engineering in Guizhou province, China. Crossing the deep Yachi River valley, its construction significantly enhanced the transportation infrastructure of a region known for its challenging topography. This bridge plays a crucial role in improving connectivity between different areas, facilitating more efficient movement of people and goods, and thereby supporting economic growth and development across the region. The impressive height of its towers and the length of its main span underscore the advancements in bridge design and construction techniques achieved in China, demonstrating the ability to overcome significant geographical obstacles to improve regional integration and accessibility.

history.html.name: Royal Gorge Bridge
history.html.title: Royal Gorge Bridge
history.html.description: The Royal Gorge Bridge is a suspension bridge over the Royal Gorge on the Arkansas River near Cañon City, Colorado, USA.
history.html.significance: The Royal Gorge Bridge, opening in December 1929, is an iconic American suspension bridge that dramatically spans the Royal Gorge of the Arkansas River in Colorado. For several decades, it held the distinction of being the world's highest bridge, a testament to the ambitious engineering of the early 20th century. Unlike many other major bridges built for transportation, the Royal Gorge Bridge was primarily conceived and constructed as a tourist attraction, aiming to capitalize on the breathtaking natural beauty of the deep canyon. Its completion spurred tourism in the region and has since become a significant landmark, drawing visitors to experience its height and the stunning views. The bridge represents an interesting intersection of engineering innovation and the early development of leisure and tourism infrastructure in the United States.

history.html.name: Zhijinghe River Bridge
history.html.title: Zhijinghe River Bridge
history.html.description: The Zhijinghe River Bridge is a concrete-filled steel tube arch bridge in Hubei province, China.
history.html.significance: The Zhijinghe River Bridge, completed in 2009, is an important concrete-filled steel tube (CFST) arch bridge located in Hubei province, China, crossing the Zhijinghe River valley. Its construction was part of a broader initiative to enhance the transportation infrastructure within a region characterized by its complex and often challenging terrain. The bridge plays a vital role in connecting various areas, facilitating more efficient movement of people and goods, and thereby supporting the economic development and social integration of the local communities. Its substantial height above the river underscores the engineering efforts to overcome geographical obstacles and improve accessibility in this part of Hubei province, contributing to the overall connectivity and progress of the region.

history.html.name: Alcantara Bridge
history.html.title: Alcantara Bridge
history.html.description: The Alcantara Bridge is a Roman arch bridge in Alcantara, Spain, spanning the Tagus River.
history.html.significance: The Alcantara Bridge, completed in 106 AD under the Roman Emperor Trajan, is a remarkable testament to Roman engineering and its enduring legacy. Located in Alcantara, Spain, it spans the Tagus River and has stood for nearly two millennia, surviving numerous wars and natural events. Its six arches, constructed from massive granite blocks without mortar, showcase the advanced construction techniques of the Roman Empire. The bridge was strategically important for connecting Norba (Cáceres) and Conimbriga (Portugal) and served as a vital communication and trade route. An inscription on the triumphal arch at its entrance proudly dedicates the bridge to Trajan and the genius of Roman engineering, highlighting its significance as a symbol of Roman power and infrastructure prowess in the Iberian Peninsula.

history.html.name: Ponte Fabricio
history.html.title: Ponte Fabricio
history.html.description: The Ponte Fabricio is one of the oldest Roman bridges in Rome, Italy, spanning the Tiber River.
history.html.significance: The Ponte Fabricio, built in 62 BC, is one of the oldest surviving Roman bridges in Rome, Italy, and stands as a remarkable example of ancient Roman engineering. Commissioned by Lucius Fabricius, the curator viarum (official in charge of roads), it connects the Campus Martius on the east bank of the Tiber River to Tiber Island in the middle. For over two thousand years, this sturdy stone bridge has facilitated movement across the river, witnessing the rise and fall of empires and the continuous development of Rome. Its two main arches, supported by a central pier with a smaller flood-relief arch, demonstrate the Romans' understanding of hydraulics and structural stability. The bridge's longevity underscores the quality of Roman construction and its enduring importance to the city's infrastructure.

history.html.name: Ponte di Tiberio
history.html.title: Ponte di Tiberio
history.html.description: The Ponte di Tiberio is a Roman bridge in Rimini, Italy, spanning the Marecchia River.
history.html.significance: The Ponte di Tiberio, construction of which began in 14 AD under Emperor Augustus and was completed in 20 AD under his successor Tiberius, is a significant Roman bridge that still stands in Rimini, Italy, crossing the Marecchia River. This robust stone structure, with its five semicircular arches, exemplifies the durability and engineering skill of the Roman Empire. It served as a crucial part of the Via Aemilia, a major Roman road connecting Piacenza to Rimini, facilitating trade and communication along the Adriatic coast. The bridge has withstood numerous floods, earthquakes, and wars over its two millennia of existence, remaining an integral part of Rimini's infrastructure and a powerful reminder of the Roman presence and influence in the region. Its well-preserved state allows us to appreciate the sophisticated construction techniques employed by Roman engineers.

history.html.name: Ponte Vecchio
history.html.title: Ponte Vecchio
history.html.description: The Ponte Vecchio is a medieval stone closed-spandrel segmental arch bridge over the Arno River in Florence, Italy.
history.html.significance: The Ponte Vecchio, rebuilt in 1345 after a devastating flood, is a unique and iconic medieval bridge spanning the Arno River in Florence, Italy. It is famous for having shops built along it, a practice that dates back to the 13th century. Originally, these shops were occupied by butchers, but over time, they were replaced by goldsmiths, jewelers, and art dealers, giving the bridge its current distinctive character. The Vasari Corridor, an enclosed passageway built in 1565 for Cosimo I de' Medici, runs above the shops, connecting the Uffizi Gallery with the Pitti Palace. The Ponte Vecchio is the only bridge in Florence spared from destruction during World War II, adding to its historical and cultural significance. It remains a vibrant hub of commerce and a beloved landmark, attracting countless visitors who come to admire its architecture and the bustling life it supports.

history.html.name: Charles Bridge
history.html.title: Charles Bridge
history.html.description: Charles Bridge is a historic bridge that crosses the Vltava river in Prague, Czech Republic.
history.html.significance: Charles Bridge, completed in 1402, is an iconic medieval bridge that gracefully spans the Vltava River in Prague, Czech Republic. Its construction began in 1357 under King Charles IV, intended to replace the Judith Bridge that had been severely damaged by floods. For centuries, it was the only bridge across the Vltava, making it a vital connection between Prague Castle and the Old Town. The bridge is renowned for its impressive Gothic architecture and the numerous Baroque statues that line its sides, added primarily in the 18th century. Over its long history, Charles Bridge has been a silent witness to many significant events in Czech history and has become a beloved symbol of Prague, attracting artists, vendors, and millions of tourists each year who stroll across its ancient stones.

history.html.name: Rialto Bridge
history.html.title: Rialto Bridge
history.html.description: The Rialto Bridge is one of the four bridges spanning the Grand Canal in Venice, Italy.
history.html.significance: The Rialto Bridge, completed in 1591, is one of the most famous and architecturally significant bridges in Venice, Italy, gracefully arching over the Grand Canal. It replaced a wooden bridge that had collapsed and for a long period was the only way to cross the Grand Canal on foot. Designed by Antonio da Ponte, the stone bridge features two inclined ramps with shops lining both sides, leading to a central portico. Its construction was a remarkable engineering feat for the time, especially considering the soft, unstable ground of Venice. The Rialto Bridge quickly became a bustling commercial hub and a vital link in the city's transportation network. Today, it remains a major landmark, attracting countless visitors who come to admire its unique design and the vibrant atmosphere of the surrounding Rialto market area, symbolizing the enduring spirit and beauty of Venice.

history.html.name: Ponte delle Torri
history.html.title: Ponte delle Torri
history.html.description: The Ponte delle Torri is a medieval bridge in Spoleto, Italy.

technical.built: Begun in the 13th century, current structure c. 1350

history.html.significance: The Ponte delle Torri, with its current impressive structure dating back to around 1350, is a remarkable medieval bridge in Spoleto, Italy. Likely built upon Roman foundations, it not only served as a vital means of crossing the deep gorge below but also as an aqueduct, carrying water to the city. Its imposing height and the ten massive arches that support it are a testament to the engineering capabilities of the medieval period. At each end, there were originally fortified towers, giving the bridge its name ('Bridge of Towers'). Over the centuries, the Ponte delle Torri has been a symbol of Spoleto's strength and strategic importance, offering breathtaking views of the surrounding landscape and standing as a powerful reminder of the city's rich history and architectural heritage.

history.html.name: Puente Romano (Córdoba)
history.html.title: Puente Romano (Córdoba)
history.html.description: The Puente Romano of Córdoba is a Roman bridge over the Guadalquivir river in Córdoba, Spain.
history.html.significance: The Puente Romano, dating back to the 1st century AD, is a remarkably well-preserved Roman bridge that spans the Guadalquivir River in Córdoba, Spain. Built during the Roman Empire, it was a crucial part of the ancient road network, connecting the city to the southern part of the Iberian Peninsula. For many centuries, it was the only bridge in Córdoba. Its robust construction, featuring 16 arches made of ashlar stone, has allowed it to withstand the test of time and the various floods of the Guadalquivir. The bridge has witnessed the city's transformations under Roman, Visigothic, and Moorish rule, and it remains a significant historical landmark, offering stunning views of the Mezquita-Cathedral and the city skyline. Its enduring presence serves as a powerful link to Córdoba's rich and layered past.

history.html.name: Anji Bridge
history.html.title: Anji Bridge
history.html.description: The Anji Bridge is the world's oldest segmental arch bridge, located in Zhao County, Hebei province, China.
history.html.significance: The Anji Bridge, completed around 605 AD during the Sui Dynasty, is the oldest segmental arch bridge in the world and a remarkable feat of ancient Chinese engineering. Designed by the craftsman Li Chun, its innovative single segmental arch design was exceptionally advanced for its time, using less material and being lighter than traditional semicircular arches, while also allowing for greater flood passage. The bridge has stood for over 1400 years, surviving numerous earthquakes and floods, a testament to the ingenuity and durability of its construction. Its elegant and efficient design influenced bridge building for centuries and remains a celebrated example of early Chinese architectural and engineering prowess.

history.html.name: Hyde Hall Bridge
history.html.title: Hyde Hall Bridge
history.html.description: The Hyde Hall Bridge is a covered bridge located in Glimmerglass State Park near Cooperstown, New York, USA.
history.html.significance: The Hyde Hall Bridge, built in 1825, is a charming covered bridge located within Glimmerglass State Park near Cooperstown, New York, USA. Constructed for George Clarke, the owner of the Hyde Hall estate, it provided a more direct route across a stream on his property. This small but historically significant covered bridge is one of the oldest surviving covered bridges in New York State. Its timber construction and simple design are characteristic of early 19th-century American covered bridges, built to protect the wooden structure from the elements and prolong its lifespan. The Hyde Hall Bridge offers a glimpse into the early transportation infrastructure of rural America and is a picturesque feature of the historic Hyde Hall estate and the surrounding landscape.

history.html.name: Danyang-Kunshan Grand Bridge
history.html.title: Danyang-Kunshan Grand Bridge
history.html.description: The Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge is the world's longest bridge. It is part of the Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railway.
history.html.significance: The Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge, opened on June 30, 2011, is an unparalleled feat of modern engineering, holding the Guinness World Record as the longest bridge in the world. Stretching an astounding 164.8 kilometers (102.4 miles), this massive viaduct is a crucial segment of the Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railway. Its construction was a monumental undertaking, involving thousands of workers and advanced engineering techniques to erect the continuous box girder structure. The bridge traverses a diverse landscape, including rivers, lakes, canals, and rice paddies in the Yangtze River Delta. Its primary purpose is to support high-speed train travel, significantly reducing journey times between two of China's most important economic and cultural centers. The Danyang–Kunshan Grand Bridge stands as a symbol of China's rapid infrastructure development and its commitment to high-speed rail technology.

history.html.name: Changhua-Kaohsiung Viaduct
history.html.title: Changhua-Kaohsiung Viaduct
history.html.description: The Changhua–Kaohsiung Viaduct is the second longest bridge in the world. It is part of the Taiwan High Speed Rail.
history.html.significance: The Changhua–Kaohsiung Viaduct, inaugurated on January 5, 2007, is the second-longest bridge in the world, an impressive piece of infrastructure that forms a significant part of the Taiwan High Speed Rail (THSR) system. Stretching 157.3 kilometers (97.7 miles) along the western plains of Taiwan, this extensive viaduct was constructed to allow high-speed trains to traverse the region efficiently, minimizing disruptions from road traffic and geographical obstacles. Its construction involved advanced techniques in building prestressed concrete box girders, designed to withstand seismic activity common in Taiwan. The viaduct has played a crucial role in connecting major urban centers along Taiwan's west coast, facilitating economic development, reducing travel times, and enhancing the overall transportation network of the island. It stands as a testament to Taiwan's engineering capabilities and its commitment to modernizing its infrastructure.

history.html.name: Tianjin Grand Bridge
history.html.title: Tianjin Grand Bridge
history.html.description: The Tianjin Grand Bridge is one of the longest bridges in the world. It is part of the Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railway.
history.html.significance: The Tianjin Grand Bridge, opened on June 30, 2011, is an impressive viaduct that forms a significant section of the Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railway. Stretching 113.7 kilometers (70.6 miles), it ranks among the longest bridges in the world. Its construction was a massive undertaking, designed to allow high-speed trains to traverse the diverse terrain of the region efficiently. Like other bridges on this high-speed line, it features a predominantly box girder structure. The Tianjin Grand Bridge plays a crucial role in facilitating rapid transportation between two of China's most important metropolitan areas, contributing significantly to economic integration and passenger convenience along this vital corridor.

history.html.name: Cangde Grand Bridge
history.html.title: Cangde Grand Bridge
history.html.description: The Cangde Grand Bridge is a long viaduct on the Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railway in China.
history.html.significance: The Cangde Grand Bridge, which opened on June 30, 2011, is another substantial viaduct that is an integral part of the Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railway in China. Extending for 105.8 kilometers (65.7 miles), it is one of the world's longest bridges. Its construction was a significant engineering endeavor, designed to support high-speed train travel across the region. Characterized by its box girder structure, the Cangde Grand Bridge efficiently navigates various geographical features. Its importance lies in its contribution to the high-speed rail network, facilitating rapid and reliable transportation between Beijing and Shanghai, thereby fostering economic and social connectivity along this major transportation artery in China.

history.html.name: Weinan Weihe Grand Bridge
history.html.title: Weinan Weihe Grand Bridge
history.html.description: The Weinan Weihe Grand Bridge is part of the Zhengzhou–Xi'an High-Speed Railway in China.
history.html.significance: The Weinan Weihe Grand Bridge, which opened on February 6, 2010, is a significant viaduct that forms a crucial part of the Zhengzhou–Xi'an High-Speed Railway in China. Stretching for 79.7 kilometers (49.5 miles), it is one of the longest bridges globally. This extensive structure was engineered to allow high-speed trains to efficiently cross the Wei River multiple times, along with other geographical features of the region. Its construction, primarily using box girder segments, showcases the advanced capabilities in high-speed rail infrastructure development in China. The Weinan Weihe Grand Bridge has played a vital role in reducing travel times and enhancing connectivity between the major cities of Zhengzhou and Xi'an, contributing to economic growth and regional integration in central China.

history.html.name: Bang Na Expressway
history.html.title: Bang Na Expressway
history.html.description: The Bang Na Expressway is a long elevated highway in Bangkok, Thailand.
history.html.significance: The Bang Na Expressway, officially known as the Burapha Withi Expressway, is a 54-kilometer (34-mile) long elevated highway in Bangkok, Thailand, which opened in March 2000. For a period, it held the title of the world's longest bridge. Constructed to alleviate ground-level traffic congestion in the bustling city, this massive infrastructure project significantly improved commuting times and transportation efficiency in the greater Bangkok metropolitan area. The expressway primarily features a prestressed concrete box girder design. Its construction was a major engineering undertaking in Southeast Asia, demonstrating the scale and ambition of infrastructure development in the region aimed at addressing urban transportation challenges and supporting economic growth.

history.html.name: Beijing Grand Bridge
history.html.title: Beijing Grand Bridge
history.html.description: The Beijing Grand Bridge is a long viaduct on the Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railway in China.
history.html.significance: The Beijing Grand Bridge, opened on June 30, 2011, is a significant viaduct that forms part of the extensive Beijing–Shanghai High-Speed Railway network in China. Stretching over 48 kilometers (approximately 30 miles), this bridge was engineered to facilitate high-speed train travel across the region. Its construction, characterized by the use of box girder structures, was a major undertaking aimed at minimizing ground-level interference and ensuring efficient and rapid transit between Beijing and Shanghai. As a key component of one of the world's longest high-speed rail lines, the Beijing Grand Bridge plays a vital role in connecting major economic and cultural centers in China, supporting both passenger and economic transport.

history.html.name: Lake Pontchartrain Causeway
history.html.title: Lake Pontchartrain Causeway
history.html.description: The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway is a pair of parallel bridges crossing Lake Pontchartrain in southern Louisiana, USA.
history.html.significance: The Lake Pontchartrain Causeway consists of two parallel precast concrete trestle bridges that cross Lake Pontchartrain in southern Louisiana, USA. The northbound span opened in 1956, followed by the longer southbound span in 1969. For a significant period, it held the Guinness World Record for the longest bridge over water. The Causeway was conceived and built to connect the north and south shores of Lake Pontchartrain, facilitating easier and faster transportation between the communities in these regions, particularly between the New Orleans metropolitan area and the north shore parishes. Its construction was a major engineering achievement, built over a large body of water with unique environmental considerations. The Causeway remains a vital transportation link and an iconic feature of the Louisiana landscape.

history.html.name: Manchac Swamp Bridge
history.html.title: Manchac Swamp Bridge
history.html.description: The Manchac Swamp Bridge is a twin concrete trestle bridge in Louisiana, USA.
history.html.significance: The Manchac Swamp Bridge, opened in 1979, is a twin concrete trestle bridge in Louisiana, USA. Spanning the Manchac Swamp, it carries Interstate 55 and is one of the longest overwater bridges in the world. Its construction was a significant engineering challenge due to the swamp's unique and often difficult environmental conditions. The bridge was built primarily with pilings driven deep into the swamp to provide stable support. It serves as a crucial transportation artery, connecting the areas north and south of the swamp and facilitating the movement of people and goods along I-55. The Manchac Swamp Bridge is notable not only for its length but also for the way it traverses a large and ecologically sensitive wetland environment.

history.html.name: Hangzhou Bay Bridge
history.html.title: Hangzhou Bay Bridge
history.html.description: The Hangzhou Bay Bridge is a long highway bridge across Hangzhou Bay in China.
history.html.significance: The Hangzhou Bay Bridge, opened on May 1, 2008, is an impressive cable-stayed bridge that crosses Hangzhou Bay in China. Stretching nearly 36 kilometers (about 22 miles), it was one of the longest trans-oceanic bridges in the world upon its completion. The bridge significantly shortened the travel distance between Shanghai and Ningbo, two major economic hubs in the Yangtze River Delta, boosting economic development and regional integration. Its construction was a monumental engineering feat, facing challenges such as complex tidal patterns, soft soil conditions, and the need to withstand typhoons and strong waves. The Hangzhou Bay Bridge features a unique S-shape design and includes a service island in the middle. It stands as a symbol of China's ambitious infrastructure projects and its advancements in long-span bridge construction over challenging marine environments.
